name: TreeSet_Comparable
protocol: ((add | addall))*; each pre-call event is checked independently, with no stateful ordering requirement.
important_note: This is a JavaMOP/RV-Monitor property rather than a CrySL rule at the supplied Crypto-API-Rules path. It checks only whether a matched value is instanceof Comparable before TreeSet calls. It does not prove successful insertion, mutual comparability, constructor/comparator choice, or runtime failure. Its broad add* pointcut is known to overmatch addAll.

events.name: add
events.condition: Observed: a pre-call matching call(* Collection+.add*(..)) whose runtime receiver is java.util.TreeSet and whose argument is bound as e. Predicate satisfied for a finding: e is not instanceof java.lang.Comparable. Because add* also matches addAll, observing .addAll(...) alone does not establish that a non-Comparable element was supplied.

events.name: addall
events.condition: Observed: a pre-call matching call(* Collection+.addAll(Collection)) whose runtime receiver is java.util.TreeSet and whose Collection argument is bound as c. Predicate satisfied for a finding: at least one iterated element elem of c is not instanceof java.lang.Comparable. Observing .addAll(...) alone is insufficient.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer a cryptographic weakness, confidentiality issue, or authentication defect from this finding.
Do not infer that java.util.TreeSet.add or addAll necessarily throws at runtime solely because the detector warns.
Do not infer that the TreeSet uses natural ordering rather than an explicit Comparator; this property does not observe construction or comparator state.
Do not infer that all existing and incoming elements are mutually comparable, that compareTo cannot throw ClassCastException, or that ordering is consistent with equals.
Do not infer that a reported addAll call necessarily contains a non-Comparable element: the broad add* pointcut can test the Collection argument itself.
Do not infer that mop.TreeSet_Comparable is a JDK runtime collection class; it is the package-qualified JavaMOP specification declaration.
semantic_scope: The verified rule observes pre-call join points for Collection add* and addAll methods only when the dynamic receiver is java.util.TreeSet. It performs runtime instanceof Comparable tests on a single bound argument or on elements iterated from an addAll Collection. The representative finding concerns org.yaxim.androidclient.widget.AutoCompleteJidEdit.setServerList; available representative source evidence indicates a TreeSet<String> receiver and a servers.addAll(dyn_elements) call.

detector_semantics.claim: The monitor produces the message "A non-comparable object is being inserted into a TreeSet object." when its local instanceof Comparable predicate fails at a matched pre-call event.
predicates: add event: target(TreeSet) AND call(* Collection+.add*(..)) AND args(e) AND !(e instanceof Comparable).
addall event: target(TreeSet) AND call(* Collection+.addAll(Collection)) AND args(c) AND there exists an iterated elem in c such that !(elem instanceof Comparable).
The representative servers.addAll(dyn_elements) shape is matched by both the broad add* pattern and the explicit addAll(Collection) pattern.
limitations: The rule has no monitor state and does not track TreeSet constructor selection, comparator presence, prior elements, insertion result, or thrown exceptions.
The source states that it does not verify mutual comparability because of performance degradation.
The source uses add*(..) rather than add(..); the archived property-db issue documents false alarms for addAll when the Collection argument itself is not Comparable.
A static detector may approximate runtime join points and instanceof tests; the representative finding does not identify the detector's exact approximation strategy.

documented_behavior: java.util.TreeSet orders elements by natural ordering or by a Comparator supplied at construction.
TreeSet.add and TreeSet.addAll may throw ClassCastException when supplied elements cannot be compared with elements already in the set.
preconditions: For natural ordering, inserted elements must implement java.lang.Comparable and be mutually comparable: relevant comparisons must not throw ClassCastException.
For a TreeSet with a non-null Comparator, inserted elements need not implement Comparable; they must instead be comparable according to that Comparator.
Null acceptance depends on the comparison mode: natural ordering rejects null, while a Comparator may or may not permit null.
unknowns: The exact Android/JDK library version used by the analyzed build is not identified.
The finding does not establish that the detector's modeled TreeSet behavior exactly follows the target platform implementation.
Representative source evidence constructs servers with new TreeSet<String>(Arrays.asList(static_list)) and does not show an explicit Comparator for that field.

security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector claims a possible violation of a collection-ordering precondition: a matched argument failed an instanceof Comparable test.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: This is an API-correctness concern. A natural-order TreeSet requires Comparable and mutual comparability, whereas a comparator-backed TreeSet can validly contain non-Comparable objects.

source_level: Confirm that the receiver is java.util.TreeSet rather than merely a Set, SortedSet, or another framework type.
For a direct add finding, establish the static and/or runtime type of the actual element argument.
For an addAll finding, distinguish the Collection argument object from the types of its elements.
Establish whether the TreeSet uses natural ordering, a null Comparator, or a non-null Comparator.
For the representative code, verify whether dyn_elements remains Collection<String> through its call chain and whether raw or unchecked uses can violate that declaration.
runtime: Observe the relevant add or addAll call and the dynamic receiver type.
For natural ordering, test comparisons against existing elements, not merely instanceof Comparable.
For comparator-backed sets, test the supplied Comparator on incoming and existing elements.
Record whether the operation returns normally, rejects the value, or throws ClassCastException or NullPointerException.
compatibility: Use TreeSet documentation and implementation behavior applicable to the deployed Java or Android runtime.
Confirm whether the reporting detector uses the archived TreeSet_Comparable.mop rule unchanged or corrects its call(* Collection+.add*(..)) pointcut.
Confirm instrumentation or analysis behavior for calls inside library code and overloaded Collection methods.

known_false_positive_shapes: A call such as servers.addAll(dyn_elements), where dyn_elements is a Collection<String> that does not itself implement Comparable, even if every inserted String is Comparable. The broad add* event can bind and test the Collection argument.
The representative AutoCompleteJidEdit.setServerList finding has this shape: servers is a TreeSet<String> and invokes servers.addAll(dyn_elements).
A TreeSet created with a non-null Comparator that validly orders instances of a class that does not implement Comparable.
A comparator-backed TreeSet that validly permits null while the rule rejects null because null is not instanceof Comparable.
Elements that implement Comparable but are not mutually comparable with existing elements are a false negative for this rule's test, not evidence that the runtime operation is safe.
unknowns: The requested Crypto-API-Rules raw URL, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/TreeSet_Comparable.crysl, was attempted and returned HTTP 404; no TreeSet_Comparable.crysl source was found there.
The verified source is instead the archived Runtime Verification property-db JavaMOP specification TreeSet_Comparable.mop.
It is not established whether the reporting detector imported the verified MOP rule verbatim, translated it, or corrected the documented addAll overmatch.
The supplied finding does not identify the exact source line or call expression in the analyzed revision, though representative upstream implementation evidence contains servers.addAll(dyn_elements).
Available evidence does not establish the dynamic contents of dyn_elements, the presence of unchecked conversion, or the deployed Android runtime's precise TreeSet behavior.
